LESSON: ORAL LITERATURE 3.1.1 SONGS/ ORAL POETRY

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: LITERATURE IN ENGLISH
Strand: Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Suggested Learning Experiences Sugg
Topic 3.1: Oral Literature 3.1.1 Songs/ Oral Poetry
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Oral Literature 3.1.1 Songs/ Oral Poetry, part of Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Suggested Learning Experiences Sugg in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 LITERATURE IN ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why do people sing songs?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. describe the features of songs for literary analysis,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Oral Literature 3.1.1 Songs/ Oral Poetry in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. discuss the types of songs for literary appreciation,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Oral Literature 3.1.1 Songs/ Oral Poetry in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. analyse the functions of songs for literary appreciation,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Oral Literature 3.1.1 Songs/ Oral Poetry in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. appreciate the value of songs in the society.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Oral Literature 3.1.1 Songs/ Oral Poetry in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. describe the features of songs for literary analysis,

   Oral Literature 3.1.1 Songs/ Oral Poetry helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. discuss the types of songs for literary appreciation,

   Oral Literature 3.1.1 Songs/ Oral Poetry helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. analyse the functions of songs for literary appreciation,

   Oral Literature 3.1.1 Songs/ Oral Poetry helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. appreciate the value of songs in the society.

   Oral Literature 3.1.1 Songs/ Oral Poetry helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. listen to an oral song from an audio or online source,

2. collaborate to discuss the features of the song and share findings in class,

3. search online or offline for features of songs and present findings on charts. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body, use adapted digital devices, assistive technology or be assisted.

4. team up to sing common songs. Learners with speech difficulties could use residual speech, hum, mime or use alternative mode of communication,

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. listen to an oral song from an audio or online source,
2. collaborate to discuss the features of the song and share findings in class,
3. search online or offline for features of songs and present findings on charts. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body, use adapted digital devices, assistive technology or be assisted.
4. team up to sing common songs. Learners with speech difficulties could use residual speech, hum, mime or use alternative mode of communication,

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Oral Literature 3.1.1 Songs/ Oral Poetry together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Digital literacy: This is promoted as the learner interacts with digital technology while searching for features of songs

from online sources.

● Learning to learn: This is nurtured as the learner carries out investigations to build on their own learning experiences when

teaming up to sing common songs.

Values:
Unity: This is developed as the learner works with others to brainstorm on the functions of songs and make notes.

Love: This is nurtured as the learner displays trustworthiness while sharing their responses with peers for review.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Citizenship: This is enhanced as the learner interacts with information on types of songs from various sources especially about

child care and protection.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. describe the features of songs for literary analysis,
2. discuss the types of songs for literary appreciation,
3. analyse the functions of songs for literary appreciation,
4. appreciate the value of songs in the society.

Remember the key question: Why do people sing songs?
